paragraphs.source_en: In the fifteenth year of Keichō, what set Tokugawa Ieyasu most at ease was the easing of relations with Osaka.

units.source_en: In the fifteenth year of Keichō, what set Tokugawa Ieyasu most at ease was the easing of relations with Osaka.

paragraphs.source_en: People said that Ieyasu spared no effort for the sons born to him in old age and doted on them beyond measure. Ieyasu ordered the daimyō to build Nagoya Castle, claiming that the annual flooding of the Gojō River around Kiyosu Castle undermined its foundations; but the excuse was so stale that any discerning observer could see he had another purpose.

paragraphs.source_en: Yet this did not mean abandoning the defense of the realm. As before, ensuring the defenses of every castle was the minimum requirement. Moreover, at strategic points in the heart of each domain, castles larger than before had to be built to accommodate shogunate forces.

units.source_en: Yet this did not mean abandoning the defense of the realm.
units.source_zh: 然而，这并不意味着对防卫家国的放弃。

paragraphs.source_zh: 然而，这并不意味着对防卫家国的放弃。和过去一样，作好各个城池的防卫，乃是最低要求。此外，居于各领地中心的要冲之地，也必筑建超过以往规模的城池，以容纳幕府军队。

paragraphs.source_en: The castle in Echigo served the same purpose. Geographically, it would become a gateway with direct routes to every part of Japan; Ieyasu stationed Matsudaira Tadateru there to guard it closely.

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu actually intended to abandon Fukushima Castle and build a great fortress comparable to Takada, but the northeast could not rival Kansai in natural conditions, nor did finances yet permit it, so the plan had to be postponed. His idea was to put Date Masamune at the center, have the Kantō and Ōu daimyō engaged at Nagoya continue assisting with the undertaking, and let himself and Shogun Hidetada watch them closely from the side.

paragraphs.source_zh: 其实，家康欲废弃福岛城，建一座与高田规模相当的大城，但就自然条件而言，东北比不得关西，财力也还不允许，故只得延期。家康的想法，是以伊达政宗为主，让参与筑名古屋城的关东与奥羽各大名在此事上继续协助，他与将军秀忠则于一旁仔细观察。

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu's sole remaining anxiety now came from the imperial court. The Emperor was at odds with Crown Prince Masahito, and several court nobles had intervened; a great upheaval seemed imminent. Perhaps the cause of this trouble arising from nowhere was that, once freed from the poverty of the age of war, the court nobles each formed their own designs and began dreaming of power again.

paragraphs.source_zh: 如今家康唯一的不安，其实来自宫中。天皇和太子政仁亲王不和，几位公卿介入其中，眼看就要掀起巨浪。导致平地生起风波的原因，也许便是公卿们从乱世的穷困境地摆脱出来后，各有打算，重新做起权力美梦。

paragraphs.source_en: When Lord Hideyoshi served as kampaku, the court nobles had not rejoiced that the realm was approaching peace; instead, they complained that he had profaned the national order. If Hideyori someday became kampaku and rose above them, while also receiving a domain worth six hundred thousand koku as a collateral house of the shogunate, it would greatly obstruct their ambitions.

paragraphs.source_en: In fact, Kiyomasa had shown extraordinary sincerity in the construction of Nagoya Castle. The daimyō had summoned great numbers of craftsmen from their domains to Nagoya, where they labored day and night. Some craftsmen molested women or caused drunken disturbances, provoking considerable resentment among the townspeople and officials. Only the men brought by Kiyomasa lived in peace with the people. Their task was to use earth from the hills around the old castle to fill the valleys and low ground.
